slides.title: SQL Playground — Help
slides.html: An in-browser SQLite environment. Databases live entirely in your browser — either in your data-root folder (via the File System Access API) or in IndexedDB as a fallback.

slides.title: The app
slides.html: This is the app as it opens. Every screenshot in this deck is captured from the running app, not drawn by hand.

slides.title: Getting started
slides.html:
1. The app opens with a scratchpad database and a small demo schema.
  2. Press Ctrl+Enter (or click Run) to execute the SQL in the editor. If you have text selected, only the selection runs.
  3. Use the left panel to manage saved databases and snippets.
  4. Use the right panel to inspect the schema, view the ER diagram, or ask the LLM assistant to write SQL for you.

slides.title: Databases
slides.html:
• Click + in the Databases side panel to create a new empty DB.
  • Click a database name to load it (unsaved work is prompted before switching).
  • Click the 📥 import icon to open a .sqlite / .db / .sqlite3 file.
  • Click the ⬇ export icon next to a DB to download it as a .sqlite file.
  • Save persists the current DB to your data root (or IndexedDB).
  • Save As… clones it under a new name.
  • The name pill in the toolbar is clickable — use it to rename the current DB.

slides.title: Editor & results
slides.html:
• Ace-powered SQL editor with syntax highlighting.
  • Run executes the whole script, or the current selection. All statements run; the last result set is shown.
  • Plan runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for the selected statement and renders it as a tree.
  • The results grid is virtualised — 100k-row result sets scroll smoothly.

slides.title: Schema & diagram
slides.html:
• Schema tab: expandable table tree. Click a column to insert its name into the editor; click the 👁 icon to SELECT * FROM … that table.
  • Diagram tab: auto-laid-out ER diagram using foreign-key constraints as edges. Based on the shared force-directed graph layout.

slides.title: LLM Assistant
slides.html:
The assistant uses the same provider / model selection as the rest of the hub. Set an API key from the toolbar key icon, and pick a model from the dropdown.

Modes:

  • Suggest query — natural-language → SQL against the current schema.
  • Draft schema — a description → a set of CREATE TABLE statements.
  • Seed data — generate INSERT statements for the current schema.
  • Explain — plain-language explanation of the SQL currently in the editor.

Each generated SQL block has To editor (replaces the editor contents) and Run (executes against the current DB) buttons.

slides.title: CSV import / export
slides.html:
• Toolbar 📄 import CSV opens a dialog to name a new table. The importer infers INTEGER / REAL / TEXT from the sample values. Existing tables with the same name are dropped.
  • Toolbar 📤 export CSV downloads the current result set.

slides.title: Snippets
slides.html:
• Type a name in the Snippets side panel and click 💾 to save the editor contents as a reusable snippet under the current DB.
  • Click a snippet to load it back into the editor.
  • Snippets follow the DB: loading a different DB swaps its snippet list.

slides.title: Tips
slides.html:
• You can quote reserved words (like "order") to use them as table names.
  • The first time you run a query, sql.js (≈1 MB WASM) is downloaded and cached by the browser.
  • The demo schema is preloaded into the scratchpad DB so SELECT statements work immediately.

slides.title: Troubleshooting
slides.html:
• "Failed to load sql.js" — check your internet connection; the WASM is loaded from cdnjs.cloudflare.com on first use.
  • "DB not found" — the database was deleted externally. Create a new DB from the toolbar.
  • "Pick a model first" — open Settings (cog), add an OpenRouter API key, and pick a model from the dropdown.
